slides.headline: Why SBI's 50 bps Forecast Is A Retail Trap
slides.title: The RBI Rate Hike Trap

slides.headline: The Illusion of Mandatory Policy
slides.card_text: Retail investors panic-sell, assuming bank research is a binding decree. In reality, institutional desks view a 25 bps forecast as a signal for yield curve re-anchoring. Commercial banks publish these hawkish projections primarily to justify widening their Net Interest Margins on floating retail loans well before actual costs rise.
slides.title: Research Notes Aren't Mandates

slides.headline: The Hidden Mechanism of Capital Extraction
slides.card_text: When banks forecast hikes, they front-run the market by repricing retail debt immediately. This creates a silent transfer of wealth from borrowers to lenders. By reacting to headlines, retail investors often lock in losses on equities while simultaneously absorbing higher interest costs on their personal floating-rate liabilities.
slides.title: How Lenders Front-Run You

slides.headline: Institutional Liquidity and Order Flow
slides.card_text: Institutional players do not dump positions based on research notes; they use the volatility caused by retail panic to accumulate quality assets at lower valuations. The 'liquidity trap' occurs when retail investors exit at the bottom, providing the necessary volume for institutional desks to rebalance their portfolios efficiently.
slides.title: Smart Capital Absorbs Panic

slides.headline: The Compounding Drag of Reactive Trading
slides.card_text: Frequent portfolio rebalancing based on macro headlines erodes capital through transaction costs and tax leakage. A 25 bps shift is statistically negligible for long-term equity compounding. Over a decade, reactive trading can reduce net returns by 15-20% compared to a disciplined, long-term buy-and-hold strategy.
slides.title: The Hidden Rebalancing Cost

slides.headline: The Non-Negotiable Institutional Rule
slides.card_text: Never reallocate your core equity holdings based on external research projections. Instead, treat every hawkish forecast as a trigger to audit your personal balance sheet. If your portfolio cannot withstand a 50 bps stress test on your floating-rate debt, your leverage, not your equity allocation, is the problem.
slides.title: Protect Your Core Portfolio

slides.headline: The Pre-Trade Verification Checklist
slides.card_text: Before acting on any macro headline: 1. Calculate the impact of a 50 bps hike on your total EMI outflow. 2. Verify if your equity holdings have pricing power to offset inflation. 3. Ensure your emergency fund covers 6 months of increased debt servicing costs. Protect your principal first.
slides.title: The Pre-Macro Stress Test
